The defendant, Ng Sui-ting, appeared in court this morning wearing a green polo shirt, beige shorts, and a black mask. The charges allege that the defendant, on 10 July and 17 August respectively, allowed a male yellow mongrel to enter the area around Yuen Long YOHO Mall without being held on a leash no longer than two metres. He faces two counts of "permitting a large dog to enter or remain in a public place".

The prosecution applied for the case to be adjourned for ten weeks before the next mention, and did not oppose bail. Acting Chief Magistrate Tang Siu-hung agreed to adjourn the case to 29 October for mention, and the defendant was granted bail.

Under the Dangerous Dogs Regulation, a conviction for "permitting a large dog to enter or remain in a public place" carries a maximum penalty of a HK$25,000 fine and three months' imprisonment.

Assistant Director of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) Ip said yesterday that if the dog owner decides to surrender the large dog to the government, the department would consider options including humane euthanasia; if the owner intends to take the dog back, the dog may be classified as a "known dangerous dog", and the court may order that the dog must wear a muzzle whenever it goes out in the future.

Kent, founder of the animal protection organisation Mochi Rescue, told FactWire that the dog owner regrets signing the abandonment form; he also said Mochi is willing to take in the dog and provide a dog trainer for behavioural rehabilitation.
